messages:
maria (PM): quick sync — starting a decision-matrix doc for choosing which kernel variant to route to at request time. want to capture launch gating and acceptance criteria so we can answer customers during previews.

 tj (Eng): SG. are we targeting explicit routing rules or model-agnostic policy (latency/cost/quality signals)?

 maria (PM): both. plan is a prioritized rule-set + fallback policy. decision matrix should include: perf delta, token cost, quality delta (eval buckets), and edge cases (long prefix, streaming, tool-calls).

 oliver (Eng-runtime): ok. my concern: we need clear SLOs per route. e.g., 99p latency < 200ms for short-context chat path. if kernel A meets cost but blows 95p, cannot roll.

 elena (SRE): +1. also include observability acceptance: histogram of kernel switches, rollback triggers when error rate increases by >2x, and ability to force route via header for debugging.

 maria (PM): acceptance checklist draft:
- canary traffic run (1%) for 24h without p99 regressions >10% vs baseline
- no increase in user-facing errors
- quantized kernel must preserve eval pass-rate >= 98% on critical prompt suite
- autoscale behavior predictable (no oscillations > 3x/min)

 tj (Eng): adding edge cases: long-context (>32k) should keep legacy kernel; streaming must not degrade token emission rate; tool-calls (function call JSON) must preserve ordering and not cut tokens.

 oliver (Eng-runtime): proposed rollout plan:
1) internal perf run (bench infra) — smoke
2) canary on internal customers (prod-tag: internal) — 12h
3) 1% stable traffic for 24h with metrics check
4) 10% for 48h
5) full rollout with staged regions

 runtime-bot: deploy started: canary job runtime-matrix/v0.1 -> cluster-beta

 elena (SRE): what about KV cache policies? decision matrix should surface cache hit-rate sensitivity: some kernels change kv key layout/ttl. we need migration plan and canary with cache-warm vs cold.

 maria (PM): good call. add steps for KV:
- verify cache key compatibility
- run synthetic cold-starts and warm-starts
- measure EVIC_RATE and miss latency
- fallback to cache-bypass on mismatch

 tj (Eng): quick note on evaluation: create three buckets — short chat, long context, and retrieval-augmented. for each, capture quality (exact-match + llr) and perf.

 oliver (Eng-runtime): also include the decision matrix columns: kernel_name, supported_seq_len, quantized(y/n), expected_p99_ms, token_cost_ratio, known_issues, fallback_variant.

 maria (PM): I'll author a PRD skeleton tonight. aim to have RFC draft by EOD Friday. volunteers to review?

 tj (Eng): i'll review perf sections.

 oliver (Eng-runtime): i'll own rollout gating and observability hooks.

 elena (SRE): happy to validate SLO checks and rollback playbook.

 maria (PM): thanks — assigning follow-ups in the doc. major customer ask: "can we guarantee no >10% latency regressions when switching to quant kernels" — should be explicit in PRD.

 tj (Eng): we should quantify: 10% at p95 or p99? customer likely cares about tail. prefer p99.

 maria (PM): noted: use p99.

 oliver (Eng-runtime): one more edge case: mixed-batched requests (short+long in same batch) — kernel selection can't harm short ones. add test.

 maria (PM): perfect. i'll post the doc link when ready. thanks all. :thumbsup:
